questions.prompt: In the previous App Router caching model, what did export const dynamic equals force-dynamic mean?

options.label: Render the page only in the browser and skip Server Components.
Render the route at request time and force segment fetches away from persistent cache.
Prebuild the route shell and cache every fetch forever.

questions.explanation: The previous-model setting forced request-time rendering and made the segment behave like force-no-store for fetch caching.

questions.prompt: Fill the migration action for Cache Components apps.
questions.template: With Cache Components, force-dynamic is usually {{blank}} because pages are dynamic by default.
questions.explanation: Official migration guidance says force-dynamic is not needed under Cache Components.

questions.prompt: Order a safe force-dynamic migration review.

items.label: Find why the flag was added
Confirm whether Cache Components is enabled
Replace broad behavior with local cache or runtime boundaries
Measure freshness and latency after removal

questions.explanation: The flag may have masked real stale data or auth behavior, so understand the intent before removing it.

questions.prompt: Match each previous-model route setting to its modern review.
questions.explanation: Cache Components moves caching policy from broad segment settings to explicit cache boundaries.

questions.prompt: A dashboard is stale after a mutation. What is the weakest fix?

options.label: Tag the cached read and invalidate that tag from the mutation.
Identify the cached function that serves stale data.
Add force-dynamic to the whole route without finding the stale cache.

questions.explanation: force-dynamic can hide the stale-cache source while throwing away useful caching for the whole route.

questions.prompt: Order the decision tree for a legacy force-dynamic route.
questions.explanation: The replacement is a precise route behavior contract, not a blind flag deletion.
